# CS 27.1305 — Powerplant instruments

> [!summary]
> CS 27.1305 lists the powerplant instruments a small rotorcraft must carry. It
> is a CS-27 specification, not a CS-E one, and the rotorcraft applicant owns
> it. The list runs in one flat sequence from (a) to (w), from carburetor air
> temperature to chip detection. Most items read an engine parameter, so the
> engine applicant supplies the signal, the connection or the limit behind
> them. Three items depend on a rating the engine applicant elects to claim.

## Requirement

The verbs below are CS-27's own. They bind the rotorcraft applicant, not the
engine applicant. See `## Bearing on this engine` for what reaches CS-E.

The paragraph opens "The following are the required powerplant instruments:"
[ext CS 27.1305]. Most items are noun phrases, so their force comes from that
lead-in and not from a verb of their own.

| Ref | Obligation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| **(a)** | A carburetor air temperature indicator, for each engine having a pre-heater that can provide a heat rise in excess of 33°C (60°F). | Required |
| **(b)** | A cylinder head temperature indicator, for each case in (b)(1), (b)(2) and (b)(3). | Required |
| **(b)(1)** | Air cooled engine. | Statement |
| **(b)(2)** | Rotorcraft with cooling shutters. | Statement |
| **(b)(3)** | Rotorcraft for which compliance with CS 27.1043 is shown in any condition other than the most critical flight condition with respect to cooling. | Statement |
| **(c)** | A fuel pressure indicator, for each pump-fed engine. | Required |
| **(d)** | A fuel quantity indicator, for each fuel tank. | Required |
| **(e)** | Means to indicate the manifold pressure, for each altitude engine. | Required |
| **(f)** | An oil temperature warning device to indicate when the temperature exceeds a safe value in each main rotor drive gearbox, including any gearboxes essential to rotor phasing, having an oil system independent of the engine oil system. | Required |
| **(g)** | An oil pressure warning device to indicate when the pressure falls below a safe value in each pressure-lubricated main rotor drive gearbox, including any gearboxes essential to rotor phasing, having an oil system independent of the engine oil system. | Required |
| **(h)** | An oil pressure indicator for each engine. | Required |
| **(i)** | An oil quantity indicator for each oil tank. | Required |
| **(j)** | An oil temperature indicator for each engine. | Required |
| **(k)** | At least one tachometer to indicate the rpm of each engine and, as applicable, the rotor speed of (k)(1), (k)(2) or (k)(3). | Required |
| **(k)(1)** | The rpm of the single main rotor. | Statement |
| **(k)(2)** | The common rpm of any main rotors whose speeds cannot vary appreciably with respect to each other. | Statement |
| **(k)(3)** | The rpm of each main rotor whose speed can vary appreciably with respect to that of another main rotor. | Statement |
| **(l)** | A low-fuel warning device for each fuel tank which feeds an engine. | Required |
| **(l)(1)** | Provide a warning to the flight crew when approximately 10 minutes of usable fuel remains in the tank. | Required |
| **(l)(2)** | Be independent of the normal fuel quantity indicating system, or be designed and constructed to meet the minimum safety objectives compatible with the most severe hazard induced by the combination of any failures of the fuel quantity indicating system and the low-fuel level warning device. | Required |
| **(m)** | Means to indicate to the flight crew the failure of any fuel pump installed to show compliance with CS 27.955. | Required |
| **(n)** | Means to indicate the gas temperature for each turbine engine. | Required |
| **(o)** | Means to enable the pilot to determine the torque of each turbine engine, if a torque limitation is established for that engine in CS 27.1521(e). | Required |
| **(p)** | For each turbine engine, an indicator to indicate the functioning of the powerplant ice protection system. | Required |
| **(q)** | An indicator for the fuel filter required by CS 27.997, to indicate the occurrence of contamination of the filter at the degree established by the applicant in compliance with CS 27.955. | Required |
| **(r)** | For each turbine engine, a warning means for the oil strainer or filter required by CS 27.1019, if it has no by-pass, to warn the pilot of the occurrence of contamination of the strainer or filter before it reaches the capacity established in accordance with CS 27.1019(a)(2). | Required |
| **(s)** | An indicator to indicate the proper functioning of any selectable or controllable heater used to prevent ice clogging of fuel system components. | Required |
| **(t)** | For rotorcraft for which a 30-second/2-minute OEI power rating is requested, provide a means to alert the pilot when the engine is at the 30-second and 2-minute OEI power levels, when the event begins, and when the time interval expires. | Required if claimed |
| **(u)** | For each turbine engine utilising 30-second/2-minute OEI power, provide a device or system for use by ground personnel which meets (u)(1) to (u)(4). | Required if claimed |
| **(u)(1)** | Automatically records each usage and duration of power in the 30-second and 2-minute OEI levels. | Required if claimed |
| **(u)(2)** | Permits retrieval of the recorded data. | Required if claimed |
| **(u)(3)** | Can be reset only by ground maintenance personnel. | Required if claimed |
| **(u)(4)** | Has a means to verify proper operation of the system or device. | Required if claimed |
| **(v)** | Warning or caution devices to signal to the flight crew when ferromagnetic particles are detected by the chip detection system required by CS 27.1337(e). | Required |
| **(w)** | For rotorcraft for which a 30-minute power rating is claimed, provide a means to alert the pilot when the engines are at the 30-minute power rating levels, when the event begins, when the time interval expires and, if a cumulative limit in one flight exists, when the cumulative time in one flight is reached. | Required if claimed |

Three rows carry Required if claimed rather than Required. Sub-points (t) and
(u) bind only where "a 30-second/2-minute OEI power rating is requested"
[ext CS 27.1305(t)], and (w) only where a 30-minute power rating is claimed
[ext CS 27.1305(w)]. The rating is elective for the engine applicant; once it is
claimed, the instrument is mandatory for the rotorcraft.

Sub-points (b)(1) to (b)(3) and (k)(1) to (k)(3) are Statement. They name the
cases in which the instrument above them is required, and impose nothing of
their own.

The text of (w) reads "a 30-minute power rower rating is claimed"
[ext CS 27.1305(w)]. The word "rower" has no counterpart in CS-29, which writes
the same condition as "a 30-minute power rating is claimed"
[ext CS 29.1305(a)(27)]. The rest of the sentence is identical in the two codes.

Sub-points (f) and (g) are limited to a main rotor drive gearbox "having an oil
system independent of the engine oil system" [ext CS 27.1305(g)]. They are not
instruments on the engine oil system.

### Where CS-29 differs

The two lists are not the same list with different labels. Six differences are
substantive for a turboshaft installation.

**Structure.** CS-27 has one flat list, (a) to (w), that applies to every small
rotorcraft. CS-29 divides its list in three: (a) for each rotorcraft, (b) for
Category A rotorcraft and (c) for Category B rotorcraft
[ext CS 29.1305(b)], [ext CS 29.1305(c)]. CS-27 has no category split, because
CS-27 has no Category A and Category B regime in this paragraph.

**Turbine engine instruments.** This is the largest gap. CS-29 requires a means
to indicate the gas producer speed for each turbine engine
[ext CS 29.1305(a)(12)], a free power turbine tachometer for each turbine engine
[ext CS 29.1305(a)(15)], a means to indicate power for each turbine engine
[ext CS 29.1305(a)(16)], and a tachometer for each engine that, combined with
the rotor tachometer, indicates rotor rpm during autorotation
[ext CS 29.1305(a)(13)]. CS-27 requires none of the four. It asks only for the
gas temperature [ext CS 27.1305(n)] and, where a torque limitation is
established, a means to determine torque [ext CS 27.1305(o)]. An engine offered
to both codes therefore supplies more indication channels under CS-29.

**Piston engine wording.** CS-29 names the reciprocating engine in each piston
item: a carburettor air temperature indicator for each reciprocating engine
[ext CS 29.1305(a)(1)], a cylinder head temperature indicator for each
air-cooled reciprocating engine together with a coolant temperature indicator
for each liquid-cooled reciprocating engine [ext CS 29.1305(a)(2)], and manifold
pressure for each reciprocating engine of the altitude type
[ext CS 29.1305(a)(5)]. CS-27 writes the same three items without naming the
engine cycle, in (a), (b) and (e). CS-27 also has no coolant temperature item.

**Gearbox oil instruments.** CS-27 limits its gearbox oil warning devices to a
main rotor drive gearbox with an oil system independent of the engine oil
system [ext CS 27.1305(f)], [ext CS 27.1305(g)]. CS-29 carries no such
condition, and reaches further: an oil pressure indicator for each
pressure-lubricated gearbox [ext CS 29.1305(a)(6)], an oil pressure warning
device for each pressure-lubricated gearbox [ext CS 29.1305(a)(7)], and an oil
quantity indicator for each oil tank and each rotor drive gearbox where the
lubricant is self-contained [ext CS 29.1305(a)(8)].

**Fuel pressure.** CS-27 requires a fuel pressure indicator for each pump-fed
engine [ext CS 27.1305(c)]. CS-29 requires an individual fuel pressure indicator
for each engine "unless the fuel system which supplies that engine does not
employ any pumps, filters, or other components subject to degradation or failure
which may adversely affect fuel pressure at the engine" [ext CS 29.1305(a)(21)].
The CS-29 relief is narrower than the CS-27 condition.

**Items CS-27 does not have at all.** CS-29 requires an indicator, warning or
caution device for an auxiliary power unit whose gas temperature, oil pressure
or rotor speed limits are being exceeded, where exceeding them can be hazardous
[ext CS 29.1305(a)(24)]. For Category A it adds an engine oil pressure warning
or a master warning device with isolation, an independent fuel pressure warning
device or the equivalent master arrangement, fire warning indicators, and, where
an OEI Training Mode is prescribed, a means to indicate the simulation of an
engine failure, the annunciation of that simulation and a representation of the
OEI power being provided [ext CS 29.1305(b)(4)]. For Category B it adds an
individual oil pressure indicator for each engine and fire warning indicators
where fire detection is required [ext CS 29.1305(c)]. CS-27 has no fire warning
item, no OEI Training Mode item and no auxiliary power unit item.

The three rating-driven items exist in both codes with the same words and
different labels. The pilot alerting duty for the 30-second and 2-minute OEI
levels is (t) here and (a)(25) in CS-29; the ground recording device is (u) here
and (a)(26); the 30-minute power alerting duty is (w) here and (a)(27). A label
must never be carried across.

## Bearing on this engine

CS 27.1305 creates no CS-E obligation. The instruments are fitted in the
rotorcraft, and the rotorcraft applicant provides them. The paragraph still
matters to the engine applicant, because most items on the list read an engine
parameter. Each one implies a connection, a signal or a declared limit that the
engine has to supply through the instructions for installation required by
[CS-E 20(d)] and the instrument list required by [CS-E 60(b)].

**Oil instruments.** The oil pressure indicator of (h), the oil temperature
indicator of (j) and the oil quantity indicator of (i) read the engine oil
system. [[CS-E 570]] supplies all three: "Each oil tank must have, or have
provision for, an oil quantity indicator" [CS-E 570(f)(2)], and provision must
be made near each oil pressure connection provided for instrumentation, to limit
the loss of fluid if a pipe fails [CS-E 570(a)(4)]. Where the sensing point
sits is engine-side work as well, and [[AMC E 60|AMC E 60(2)(a)]] governs it.

**Oil filter warning.** Sub-point (r) asks for a warning means for the oil
strainer or filter, for each turbine engine, where the filter has no by-pass
[ext CS 27.1305(r)]. [[CS-E 570]] carries the engine side of that condition: if
the most critical main oil filter has no by-pass, it must have "provision for
appropriate indication to the flight crew of impending blockage"
[CS-E 570(b)(2)], and where a by-pass exists, indication of by-pass operation
must be provided for maintenance action [CS-E 570(c)(2)]. The two paragraphs
divide on the same by-pass test.

**Fuel instruments.** The fuel pressure indicator of (c) reads the engine fuel
inlet, and [[CS-E 560]] requires provision near each fuel pressure connection
provided for instrumentation, to limit fluid loss if a pipe fails
[CS-E 560(f)]. The engine's own filter indication duty is separate from (q): it
is the impending blockage indication of [CS-E 560(b)(2)], to the flight crew or
to the maintenance crew.

Sub-points (m) and (q) name CS 27.955 and CS 27.997, and (r) names CS 27.1019.
Those are airframe points, and this vault does not hold them in sliced form.
The reference is recorded and not followed.

**Speed, temperature and torque.** The engine tachometer of (k), the gas
temperature of (n) and the torque determination means of (o) are the core
turboshaft channels. [[CS-E 60|CS-E 60(b)]] requires the engine applicant to
list the instruments necessary for control of the engine and to state the
overall limits of accuracy and transient response required of them.
[[CS-E 40|CS-E 40(g)]] then requires those limits to be taken into account in
determining the engine performance and operating limitations, and
[[CS-E 20|CS-E 20(e)]] requires the performance data the rotorcraft applicant
needs to use them.

**Ice protection indication.** Sub-point (p) asks for an indicator of the
functioning of the powerplant ice protection system. On the engine side this is
the general provision duty of [CS-E 60(a)], and
[[AMC E 60|AMC E 60(1)]] names "indication of engine ice protection system
activation" as an example of instrumentation that may be required for aircraft
certification. The engine operating obligation in icing is [[CS-E 780]], which
is a functioning requirement and not an instrument requirement.

**Chip detection.** Sub-point (v) requires the warning or caution devices; the
detection system itself is required elsewhere in CS-27 and is not sliced here.
CS-E imposes no chip detection instrument. It does assume the hardware:
[[AMC E 570|AMC E 570(4)]] states that, in complying with CS-E 570(a)(2),
"access points include, but are not limited to, Magnetic Chip Detectors and
gearbox access cover plates". The engine applicant therefore declares the
detector as an interface under [CS-E 20(d)], and the signalling is the
rotorcraft's.

**OEI alerting and recording.** Sub-points (t) and (u) run parallel to
[[CS-E 60|CS-E 60(d)]], which this engine triggers because `engine_profile.md`
declares 30-Second OEI and 2-Minute OEI Power. [[AMC E 60]] already sets out how
the two sides map onto each other, including the reset authority and the
maintenance alerting duty that CS-E adds. That account is not repeated here.

**30-minute power alerting.** `engine_profile.md` declares Rated 30-Minute Power
under [[CS-E 40|CS-E 40(b)(4)]], so sub-point (w) applies to a CS-27
installation of this engine. No CS-E sub-point mirrors it: CS-E 60(d) reaches
only the 30-Second and 2-Minute OEI levels [CS-E 60(d)]. The engine-side duty is
therefore the general one — provision for the instrumentation necessary to
ensure operation within the engine operating limitations [CS-E 60(a)] — plus the
30-minute limitations themselves, and the cumulative limit in one flight if the
applicant sets one, delivered through [CS-E 20(d)].

Several items reach no CS-E obligation at all. The carburetor air temperature
indicator of (a), the cylinder head temperature indicator of (b) and the
manifold pressure means of (e) are piston engine instruments; CS-29 states that
explicitly for the same three items [ext CS 29.1305(a)(1)],
[ext CS 29.1305(a)(2)], [ext CS 29.1305(a)(5)]. A turboshaft produces none of
those parameters. The fuel tank instruments of (d) and (l) and the fuel system
heater indicator of (s) belong to the aircraft fuel system. The gearbox oil
warning devices of (f) and (g) belong to the rotor drive system, whose testing
regime is [[CS 27.927]].

[VERIFY: whether a torque limitation is established for this engine in
CS 27.1521(e), which is what makes the torque determination means of (o)
required. `engine_profile.md` does not record a declared engine torque limit,
and CS 27.1521 is not held in sliced form.]

[VERIFY: whether the installation is certificated under CS-27 or CS-29. The two
instrument lists differ in substance, above all in the turbine engine channels
CS-29 adds. [[CS-E 30]] carries the same open item.]
